Compute Weighted TF-coactivity Network Analysis (WTCNA)

compute.WTCNA.Rd

Construct a weighted signed or unsigned network using TF activity to cluster protein regulators into modules that share similar activity patterns. Each TF module will have a sample-level score represented by the eigengene of the module.

Usage

compute.WTCNA(
  tfs,
  batch = NULL,
  network_type = "signed",
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  min_module_size = 5,
  corr_mod = 0.9,
  corr_type = "spearman",
  verbose = TRUE,
  file_name = NULL,
  soft_power = NULL,
  consensus_quantile = 0,
  return = TRUE
)

Arguments

tfs

Matrix of TF activity (samples x TFs), scaled or not: the TFs are standardized (within each cohort with batch) to compute the module eigengenes, and the other steps use correlations, which do not depend on the scaling. With batch, the TF activities of all the cohorts, each computed within its cohort (as CellTFusion() does).

batch

(Optional) A vector with the cohort of each sample, in the row order of tfs; if it is named, it is matched to the samples by name instead. It is always treated as categorical. If given, consensus TF modules are built across the cohorts (see Details) and module eigengenes are computed and scaled within each cohort. Default is NULL (single cohort); a vector with only one cohort is treated the same way.

network_type

Network type: "signed" (default) or "unsigned".

clustering_method

Linkage method of the hierarchical clustering of the TFs (stats::hclust()), applied to the TOM dissimilarity (1 - topological overlap) between TFs, or to the consensus TOM dissimilarity in batch mode. Default is "ward.D2" (WGCNA's own default is "average": two groups of TFs are joined according to the average dissimilarity between their TFs).

min_module_size

Minimum number of TFs per module. Default is 5.

corr_mod

Correlation threshold (0-1): modules whose eigengenes have a correlation (of type corr_type) above it are merged. In batch mode, the correlation is computed on the eigengenes of all the samples, scaled within each cohort. Default is 0.9.

corr_type

Correlation used to pick the soft-threshold power, build the adjacency matrix, merge modules and compute the proportion of variance explained: "spearman" (default) or "pearson", in single-cohort and batch mode. The module eigengene is always the first principal component of the module's TF activities.

verbose

Logical; whether to print the function messages. Default is TRUE.

file_name

Optional character suffix used when writing WTCNA outputs (CSV files and, in single-cohort mode, the diagnostic plots Soft_Threshold_<file_name>.pdf, Gene_dendrogram_and_module_colors_<file_name>.pdf and Gene_dendrogram_and_module_colors_after_merging_<file_name>.pdf).

soft_power

Optional numeric value specifying the soft-thresholding power used to build the adjacency matrix (one value per cohort, in the order the cohorts first appear in batch, in batch mode). If NULL, the lowest power whose scale-free fit \(R^2\) reaches 0.9 is chosen automatically (the power with the best fit if none reaches 0.9, with a message).

consensus_quantile

Numeric between 0 and 1 (batch mode only). For each pair of TFs, the consensus topological overlap is this quantile of its (calibrated) topological overlaps across the cohorts. With 0 (default), the minimum: two TFs are close only if they are close in every cohort, the strictest choice, which removes more TF relationships as more cohorts are added. Higher values are less strict: with K cohorts, consensus_quantile = k / (K - 1) takes the (k + 1)-th lowest value, so two TFs are close if they are close in all cohorts but k (e.g. 0.25 with 5 cohorts: in at least 4 of them); 0.5 is the median.

return

Logical, whether to save output plots, the module list (Results/TFs_modules_<file_name>.csv) and the module matrix (Results/TF_module_matrix_<file_name>.csv, with the sample names as row names) to "Results/" (without file_name, TFs_modules.csv and TF_module_matrix.csv). Default is TRUE.

Value

A named list with:

  • TFs module matrix: Scaled module eigengenes (samples x modules), in the row order of tfs.

  • TFs colors: Vector of module colors assigned to each TF ("grey" for TFs not assigned to any module).

  • TFs per module: List of TF names in each module.

  • Proportion of variance: Variance explained per module (single-cohort mode only).

  • TFs_matrix: The TF activity matrix used (a list of per-cohort matrices in batch mode, in the order the cohorts first appear in batch).

  • Network parameters: A list with the soft-thresholding power(s) used (soft_power, one per cohort in batch mode), network_type and corr_type, used by identify_hub_TFs(), and in batch mode consensus_quantile.

Details

TFs that WGCNA does not assign to any module (color "grey") are not a module: they are left out of the module matrix and of TFs per module, with a message.

In batch mode, the modules are built with the same steps as in single-cohort mode, on a consensus network:

  1. the samples are split by cohort, and a soft-thresholding power is chosen for each cohort;

  2. the adjacency and the topological overlap matrix (TOM) are computed in each cohort, with its own power;

  3. the TOMs are calibrated to a common scale as in WGCNA::blockwiseConsensusModules(): each TOM is raised to the power that makes its 0.95 quantile equal to that of the first cohort;

  4. the consensus TOM is, for each pair of TFs, the consensus_quantile quantile of its calibrated TOMs across cohorts;

  5. the TFs are clustered on 1 - consensus TOM with clustering_method and the tree is cut with the same dynamic tree cut as in single-cohort mode;

  6. the module eigengenes are computed and scaled within each cohort, and the modules are merged as in single-cohort mode (see corr_mod); merged scores are scaled within each cohort again.

Unlike WGCNA::blockwiseConsensusModules(), the TFs of each module are not filtered or reassigned afterwards by their module membership (as in single-cohort mode). The diagnostic plots are only saved in single-cohort mode.

References

Langfelder, P., & Horvath, S. (2008). WGCNA: an R package for weighted correlation network analysis. BMC Bioinformatics, 9, 559. https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-9-559

Examples


data("tfs.tuto")
network <- compute.WTCNA(tfs.tuto, corr_mod = 0.9, return = FALSE)
